title: Dynamical transition in non-Hermitian Chern insulator
authors: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Yuan-Hang Ren, Ming Lu, Hua Jiang
abstract: We unveil a peculiar dynamical transition for the propagation of wave packets in non-Hermitian Chern insulators, where the evolution of the topological wave packets at the edge is not solely determined by the topological Chern number. Unlike the Hermitian Chern insulator, where a wave packet initiated at the edge propagates along the system boundary, here it may instead penetrate into the bulk. This behavior is attributed to the competition between the localization induced by conventional topology and the non-Hermitian skin effect. Specifically, when the former dominant, the wave packet will evolve along the boundary; otherwise, it will spread into the bulk. These features demonstrate that while the generalized-Brillouin zone framework reliably predicts topological phase transitions, it does not on its own specify the dynamical transitions.
summary: This work analyzes wave packet dynamics in non-Hermitian Chern insulators, revealing a dynamical transition that is independent of the system's bulk topological invariant. The competition between the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect and intrinsic topological localization dictates whether the wave packet remains confined to the edge or spreads into the bulk.
main_problem: The paper investigates a dynamical transition in non-Hermitian Chern insulators, showing that wave packet evolution is not solely dictated by the topological Chern number.
main_result: The system exhibits two distinct dynamical regimes—edge propagation or bulk spreading—whose transition line is distinct from the topological phase transition predicted by generalized-Brillouin zone theory.
method: The study uses wave packet tracking, analyzing the evolution governed by the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, and comparing the resulting dynamics to topological invariants like the Chern number.
model_or_system: The system is a non-Hermitian Chern insulator, modeled by a specific Hamiltonian involving Pauli matrices and parameters related to hopping and non-Hermiticity ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Wave packet center location ($R_c(t)$), a diagnostic index $P$ (1 for edge, 0 for bulk), the Chern number ($C$), and the localization coefficient ($\lambda$).
important_parameters: Non-Hermiticity strength ($\gamma$), topological parameters ($m, v$), and the ratio $ eta_-^i /  eta_+^i$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the wave packet evolution formalism and assumes the applicability of the similarity transformation for analyzing edge states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram separating dynamical regimes (edge vs. bulk) and explicitly plot the distinct dynamical transition line against the topological transition line, showing their inconsistency.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the non-Hermitian model and the wave packet evolution. It then contrasts the topological prediction (GBZ theory) with the actual dynamical behavior, deriving the condition for the dynamical transition based on the competition between NHSE and intrinsic localization.
why_interesting: The explicit distinction between topological invariants (like Chern numbers) and dynamical properties (like wave packet spreading) is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where dissipation or gain is present, suggesting that simple topological characterizations are insufficient.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: (a) The phase diagram. The topologically trivial white region with Chern number C = 0 is separated with the topologically nontrivial gray and blue regions, by the red curve predicted by the GBZ theory. The solid blue curve delineates the distinct dynamical regimes marked in (b) and (c), where the wave packets evolve along the boundary in (b) , and spread into the bulk in (c).

FIG. 2: (a) and (b) are the time evolutions of wave packet |ψ(r, t)| with boundary and bulk type evolutions, respectively. Note that they are both in the topological region, as marked in (d) with red and blue squares. (c) The variation of P and Chern number C for two representative γ’s, showing clear deviation for non-Hermitian case. (d) The plot of P and C versus m and γ with system size Nx = Ny = 30. The red dashed line is the topological phase transition line based on the GBZ theory. The solid green line represents the dynamical transition line given by Eq. (19). The parameters are v = tx = ty = 1 and γx = γy = γ, with others marked in the figure accordingly.

FIG. 3: (a) A schematic illustrating the method for obtain- ing the topological edge states of H, using the transformed Hermitian Hamiltonian H = S−1HS and its eigenfunction φH as the intermediate step. (b) A typical plot of the edge state with γ = 0.1 and m = 1.8. (c) The variation of the bottom edge states along the white dashed line marked in (b) for γ ∈[0, 0.6]. (d) The red dots are the slope of the edge states in (c), and the blue solid line is the analytical curve λ = ln βy −κy. Other parameters are m = 1.8, v = 1 and γx = γy = γ.

FIG. 4: Schematic plot of the sample. The dashed blue lines represent bottom edge states with |ψ| ∝e[ln(βy)−κy]y. Here, ln(βy) are induced by the NHSE. κy is the intrinsic localization of edge states originating from the nontrivial Chern numbers. (a) is the Hermitian cases with ln(βy) = 0. (b) and (c) mark the typical edge and bulk states with ln(βy) −κy < 0 and ln(βy) −κy > 0, respectively.

FIG. 5: (a) and (b) are the time evolutions of wave packet |ψ(r, t)| with boundary and bulk type evolutions, respectively. The red dots mark the wave packet centers with maximum values of |ψ(r, t)|. (c) and (d) The variation of rc(t) versus t. The corresponding index P are noted in the figures. The parameters are the same as those in the main text. The sample sizes are Nx × Ny = 40 × 40.
